Airport security lines: I went through airport security, and they asked me to remove my belt. I said, “That’s fine, but I have to warn you, I’m also carrying *emotional baggage*.”
Endless Zoom meetings: I’ve started moisturizing my face mid-meeting — not for the camera, just fighting the existential dryness of back-to-back Zoom calls.
First dates: First dates are like job interviews where both people are lying about how much they like the city.
Smart home devices (like a Roomba or Ale: I bought a Roomba to clean my place, but it just keeps rolling over the same Cheerio for hours like it's trying to negotiate with it.
Going to the gym for the first time: I went to the gym for the first time and immediately got a six-pack... of Gatorade.
Customer service phone menus: Every customer service menu starts with "Press 1 if you're a human" — and I die a little each time.
Trying to eat healthy/Dieting: I tried to eat healthy, so I bought a salad… then I ruined it trying to make it taste like the other stuff I’m not supposed to eat. Turns out, ranch dressing is the gateway drug to diabetes.
The behavior of cats vs. dogs: Cats spend hours staring at a wall like they're solving the mystery of the universe, then suddenly sprint away like they've cracked it. Dogs just stare at the wall until they're convinced it owes them a treat.
Self-checkout machines at the grocery st: The self-checkout machine asked me to "please scan the next item," and I just stood there like, "Ma’am, we both know this is *your* job."
Insomnia and trying to fall asleep: I lay in bed staring at the ceiling, wondering if sleep is just a rumor my brain made up to torture me.
Buying things you don't need online: I bought a life-sized cardboard cutout of a cactus online... now my apartment's just a desert of regret.
Awkward family gatherings: Thanksgiving dinner with all the relatives is like a horror movie where the killer is just really bad boundaries.
Streaming service algorithms (e.g., Netf: I hate how my streaming service recommends shows because every time I watch something, it’s like the algorithm says, “Ah, you’re into *this*? Here, watch it again, but with a slightly different logo.”
Coffee shop baristas and complicated ord: I went to a café where the barista asked if I wanted oat milk or almond milk. I said, “Just regular milk,” and she looked at me like I’d asked for a time machine.
Commuting in heavy traffic: Every time I get stuck in traffic, I imagine the GPS voice saying, "Take a deep breath... for once, there's literally nowhere to go."
Job interviews: I went to a job interview where they said, "We value honesty above all." So I told them I’d never worked a day in my life and set my resume on fire. They’re still deciding if I’m a rebel... or just a liability.
Keeping houseplants alive: I bought a cactus to learn responsibility — now I'm just waiting for it to die so I can feel something.
Forgetting passwords: I tried to reset my password, but I forgot the answer to my security question... which was "What's your favorite color?" Turns out, I'm colorblind *and* identity-crisis-level confused.
High school reunions: You know you're getting old when the only thing classier than your high school reunion is the ambulance ride to it.
Assembling flat-pack furniture (e.g., IK: I tried assembling IKEA furniture once... turns out the hardest part was finding the part of my soul that still believed in clear instructions.
Tech support/Helping parents with techno: "Tech support told me to turn my router off and on again… which is exactly what my parents say when I complain about *them.*"
Alarm clocks and waking up early: I hate alarm clocks — they’re the only coworkers who get paid nothing, yet still call you names like “failure” when you hit snooze.
The culture of social media influencers: I love how influencers act surprised when their 15th unboxing video gets 200 million views — honey, we’ve seen you open a box before, we just never cared that much.
Cryptocurrencies or \"Tech Bros\": I tried investing in cryptocurrency, but all I got was this lousy NFT of a cat wearing sunglasses — and even it thinks I’m a loser.
Going to the dentist: Going to the dentist is the only time I let someone stick their finger in my mouth... and it's *still* weird.
Moving to a new apartment: Moving to a new apartment is like being a human Tetris game—except the boxes are all labeled “miscellaneous,” and gravity’s out to get you.
Annoying neighbors: I’ve got one neighbor who insists on vacuuming at 3 a.m. Either he’s fighting a war against invisible dirt, or he’s trying to summon the ghost of Karen Carpenter.
Overpacking for a vacation: I packed so much for my vacation, I had to check a bag just for the guilt.
Swipe right on a guy whose bio is just "I’m like pizza—even when I’m bad, I’m good." Turns out he was allergic to commitment and kept topping my emotions with olives.
Public transportation/Subways: Subways are great until you realize you're not stuck in traffic—you're the traffic.
Wedding planning: I told my fiancée I’d take care of the wedding music. She said, “Great, just make sure it’s not all funeral songs.” I said, “You mean *our* song isn’t ‘My Heart Will Go On’?”
Autocorrect text message fails: My phone changed “I’ll be there in five” to “I’ll be there in fries.” Boss hasn’t trusted me since.
Procrastination: I told my brain, "Let's do this thing," and my brain replied, "Challenge accepted... by the part of me that naps."
Group chats that never stop buzzing: Group chats are like a haunted house — the notifications never stop *dinging*, but somehow the only thing ghosting you is the guy who promised to bring snacks.
The cost of living/Being broke: I tried to save money by buying a cheap mattress, now I wake up feeling like I got mugged by a cloud.
Getting a bad haircut: I got a haircut so bad, I’m considering joining a cult just to have an excuse to wear a hat 24/7.
Overly complicated modern fitness trends: I tried that new fitness trend where you lift groceries while doing lunges through an IKEA showroom — turns out, the only thing I'm building is a restraining order.
People who talk at the movie theater: If you're the person who narrates the movie for the entire theater, you're not a moviegoer — you're a podcast.
Cooking disasters: I tried to make a soufflé once... it collapsed faster than my willpower at a buffet.
Small talk about the weather: "Talking about the weather is just adults doing improv comedy with a script written by disappointment."
Modern fashion trends: I tried to get into the latest fashion trend where people pay extra for holes in their clothes. Got real excited until I realized the holes were *in* the pants, not *in* the bank account.
Waiting in doctors' offices: "Waiting in a doctor's office is the only time I'd trade my smartphone for a magazine from 2003 with a missing corner."
Getting older/Turning 30: Turning thirty is like getting a software update—you didn’t ask for it, you’re not sure what changed, but now everything feels slower and you’re suddenly obsessed with backups.
Video game culture: I love when people say “I’m playing hard mode” like it’s a personality trait.
Corporate buzzwords (e.g., \"Synergy\"): "Synergy" is just what they call it when three managers stare at the same problem and no one does anything.
Dealing with landlords: I asked my landlord if the apartment included a gym, and he said, "No, but the stairs are free."
Astrological signs/Horoscopes: I checked my horoscope, and it said today is a great day to reconnect with someone from your past—so I texted my ex. Turned out, the universe meant your *dentist*.
People who overshare online: I follow this guy on social media who posts everything—like, *everything*. Yesterday he live-streamed his colonoscopy and made a TikTok with the anesthesia voiceover.
Veganism or extreme dietary restrictions: I tried being vegan for a month—now I’m just a guy who spends 45 minutes reading restaurant menus like I’m solving a crime.
Trying to assemble a tent/Camping: Every time I try to assemble a tent, it's like the poles are playing hide-and-seek... and the instructions are written in hieroglyphs.
